text:
ben: heads-up — today’s firewall hardening rollout in eu-west quota'ed outbound flows and we just hit a chain reaction: secrets-proxy calls are being rejected, audit ingestion spiked, and a bunch of GPU nodes failed their post-boot attest. seeing ~120 node join errors in the last 8m. :warning:
alice: can you paste the join error? we need the exact failure to confirm it's firewall vs IAM throttling
ben: logs: `node-173: failed to fetch /v1/bootstrap/token -> 403 from secrets-proxy (egress:REJECT)` then the agent retries and hits audit-ingest QPS which trips backpressure -> 429s
carol: confirmed similar in ap-south. firewall L7 rule tightened to drop packets to secrets-proxy IPs unless tagged. someone flipped the new default-deny micropolicy at 08:12 UTC.
dave: I saw the change — it was to block unknown outbound flows from staging after the audit incident. the rule had an overly broad CIDR that included our regional proxy pool.
maya: sec-bot alerted us, tagging security. sec-bot: ALERT: fw-default-deny rollout (rule ID fw-2026-07) increased dropped flows to secrets-proxy by 22x and audit ingestion backlog increased 15GB/min.
sec-bot: recommended mitigation: add a temporary allowlist for secrets-proxy frontends + enable audit-chain-sampling 20% until backlog drains.
ben: mitigation plan proposal: 1) add allowlist for secrets-proxy VIPs (5 min change) 2) throttle node bootstrap retries to reduce stampede 3) flip audit sampling to 20% 4) follow with a narrow fw rule update (IP-tag based) — agree?
alice: +1. I'll open the emergency PR to add the VIPs to the allowlist and add a short runbook note.
carol: while we do that, we should also gate new node joins in eu-west so we don't waste GPU warm pools. enable maintenance mode on the autoscaler?
dave: setting autoscaler to manual, draining join queue now. command: `./opsctl autoscaler set-mode eu-west manual --reason "fw rollback in progress"`
ben: deploy-bot: rollback check failed for fw-2026-07 (conflict with change set cs-8912) — manual intervention required.
maya: security asks: do not revert the entire hardening. prefer allowlist + IAM fix. audit-team: we need to preserve logs for compliance; sampling must be documented and reversible.
carol: cost tradeoff: if we let nodes keep retrying, warm pools will spin up and cost us ~ $2.4k/hr in spare GPU capacity. temporary allowlist should drop retries and save that.
alice: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/5123 — adds allowlist, updates runbook, and a short TTL of 1h. please review quick.
dave: applied autoscaler manual mode. reducing incoming node join concurrency to 4/s via `wfm throttle`
ben: alice can you coordinate with audit team to toggle sampling? also add a notice to infra-status channel so app owners don't panic.
alice: pinged @audit-team and posted infra-status message. audit-team replied ok with 20% for 45m and will archive the change for compliance.
maya: Security asks we rotate the secrets-proxy client certs if any unauthorized hits were observed. any evidence of replay/unauthorized decrypt?
ben: not that we've seen — failures are 403s from firewall, not decrypt errors. still, let's queue cert rotation in the postmortem if needed.
carol: after allowlist applied node join success rate jumped from 18% -> 94% within 3 min. backlog drained.
dave: autoscaler set back to normal. warm pools will scale down over the next 10m.
alice: follow-up actions (short): - narrow fw rule to use subnet tags (todo: infra-policy PR) - add secrets-proxy VIPs to regional host-tag mapping - document sampling incident in compliance ticket CT-8742 - propose long term: egress service registry to avoid big CIDR rules
maya: security action items (short): - review fw change approval flow to avoid broad CIDR rollouts - require a canary window for default-deny changes - verify there were no unauthorized accesses (audit-team)
ben: thanks all. we avoided a full rollback, nodes are healthy, and costs are already trending down. will author an incident note and link the PRs + metrics. :white_check_mark:
alice: FYI I'll also run a quick script to emit the join/error histogram for the postmortem: `python tools/join_hist.py --since 1780012000 --until now`
carol: closing the thread after we file CT-8742 and the postmortem doc. good ops coordination. :thumbsup:
